title: Takopi's Original Sin
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Takopi, a cheerful octopus-like alien from the Happy Planet, lands on Earth to spread happiness and befriends Shizuka, a bullied and neglected 9-year-old. When his cute 'Happy Gadgets' fail to understand human pain, a series of time loops leads to a child's suicide, a killing and a cover-up among fourth graders. A short, two-volume story with a cute art style and very dark themes.
life_message: It holds up listening to and understanding another person's pain, rather than imposing quick fixes, as the beginning of real help.

content.note: A child is accidentally killed and the body hidden; a parent attacks her daughter, who kills her in self-defense (Wikipedia).
Child abuse, cover-up and paranoia; ANN reviewers note heavy suffering (Wikipedia; Tragedy signal).
A parent's affair drives the bullying; no sexual content noted (Wikipedia).
A 9-year-old's suicide shown at the start, a second child's suicide in another timeline, severe bullying (Wikipedia; MangaUpdates Suicide/s, Bullying; AniList Bullying 93%).
Suicide method via a gadget, hiding a body, bullying, all among young children (Wikipedia; MangaUpdates).

dominant: Secular humanism (empathy), Moralistic therapeutic deism (shallow happiness critiqued), Existentialism

delivery.evidence: ANN manga guide split: MrAJCosplay says the second half pushes its message with a broad brush; Farris says its heart is right, ending contrived.

personified.ideology: quick-fix happiness that misreads real pain

delivery.note: The message about listening to pain becomes overt late in the story, and one reviewer finds that push convenient.

winners_losers: Takopi gives himself up so the girls can start over, and Shizuka and Marina are shown as victims rather than villains. Sympathy goes to children failed by adults, and to empathy over quick fixes.
